equation_request.abstract: The Quantum Fourier Transform offers an interesting way to perform arithmetic operations on a quantum computer. We review existing Quantum Fourier Transform adders and multipliers and comment some simple variations that extend their capabilities. These modified circuits can perform modular and non-modular arithmetic operations and work with signed integers. Among the operations, we discuss a quantum method to compute the weighted average of a series of inputs in the transform domain. One of the circuits, the controlled weighted sum, can be interpreted as a circuit to compute the inner product of two data vectors.

specification.problem: Reconstruct QFT-based (Draper-style) quantum arithmetic: adders and multipliers, modular and non-modular, with signed integers, including a controlled weighted sum that computes a weighted average or inner product of data vectors in the transform domain.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Small finite instance: QFT adder of a classical constant or register into a register, and a controlled weighted sum as an inner-product accumulator. Only the abstract's qualitative claims are supported; circuit details are background or assumed.

symbols.meaning: number of qubits in the target register
quantum Fourier transform on n qubits
weights and data inputs of the weighted sum

equations.label: QFT definition
equations.justification: Standard QFT definition underlying QFT arithmetic; the abstract only names the QFT.

equations.label: QFT addition
equations.description: Addition by phase rotations in the transform domain
equations.justification: Standard Draper adder; the abstract says QFT adders are reviewed but gives no formula.
assumptions: Phi(a) is the diagonal phase-rotation unitary with entries exp(2 pi i a k/2^n)

equations.label: Controlled weighted sum
equations.description: Inner product of weight vector and data vector accumulated in the output register
equations.abstract_quote: the controlled weighted sum, can be interpreted as a circuit to compute the inner product of two data vectors
equations.justification: The abstract states the inner-product interpretation; the exact form is inferred.

registers.name: x
registers.size: m*n qubits (m data inputs of n qubits each, assumed)
registers.role: data register holding inputs x_i, used as controls

registers.name: acc
registers.role: accumulator register for the sum, held in Fourier basis during accumulation

specification.initial_state: |x>|0>^n with x a computational-basis data input and acc initialized to zero (assumed)

steps.description: Apply QFT on the accumulator register acc to enter the transform domain.

For each i and each bit j of x_i, apply a controlled phase rotation on acc by angle 2*pi*w_i*2^j/2^n, controlled on bit j of x_i, so the phase accumulates sum w_i x_i (assumed Draper-style construction).
Apply inverse QFT on acc to return to the computational basis, giving |x>|sum w_i x_i mod 2^n>, i.e. the inner product.

specification.measurement: After the inverse QFT, measure acc (n qubits) in the computational basis. For a computational-basis input the outcome is deterministic and encodes S = sum w_i x_i mod 2^n. For superposed inputs, outcomes are sampled according to input amplitudes, and x can be measured jointly. Shot count is assumed and unspecified.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Convert the bitstring to an integer S in [0,2^n); for signed values use two's complement. The result is valid only if 2^n exceeds the range of the true sum. For a weighted average, divide S by the sum of weights (or shift if weights are pre-scaled to sum to 2^k); this is an assumed procedure. For superposed inputs, histogram over shots.
assumptions: Draper-style QFT adder underlies the paper's circuits
Weights w_i are classical constants compiled into rotation angles
Signed integers use two's complement mod 2^n
Weighted average needs separate normalization, e.g. weights pre-scaled to sum to a power of 2 (assumed)
Measurement is in the computational basis of acc after the inverse QFT; shot count unspecified
Overflow is avoided by choosing n large enough for the true sum range
Multiplier and modular variants are not reconstructed; only the weighted-sum instance is covered
missing_information: Exact circuits for modular, signed, and multiplier variants
Gate-level details of the controlled weighted sum and modular variants are not in the abstract
The abstract does not describe measurement or readout, nor whether the weighted average is read in the transform domain or after the inverse QFT
The abstract gives no shot counts or error analysis
